newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power firm, higher demand expected.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power firm, higher demand expected.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. held firm amid expectations of cooler weather and higher demand in the Pacific Northwest, market sources said Thursday.
"Loads have not really picked up yet, but they are expected to," said one Oregon trader.

A lack of next-day surplus power offers from the Bonneville Power Administration was also seen as a bullish signal by traders who noted that continued spot sales by the federal agency would probably drive prices lower.
Firmer spot natural gas prices were also cited as supportive of cash power prices in the West.
Firm on-peak power for Friday at the Califoria-Oregon border (COB) was last quoted $22.50-23.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), up slightly from $22.50-22.75 on Wednesday.
Off-peak COB was also higher at $18.50-19.00.
Next-day Mid-Columbia quotes were $19.50-20.00, compared with $18.50-20.00.
Another trader predicted cooler Northwest temperatures next week would push cash power prices up about $1.00 per MWh.
Firm on-peak Palo Verde was quoted $20.00-20.50 per MWh for Friday deliveries, little changed from Wednesday. Four Corners was quoted $21.00-21.50, compared with $20.00-21.00.
December COB was quoted $24.10-24.35 at midday, up sharply from $23.00-23.50 early Wednesday. Palo Verde for December was last quoted $22.20-22.50, up from $21.50-22.00 late Wednesday.
